verses.text: Here’s the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD.
“Listen to the words of this covenant and pass them on to the people of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem.
Tell them the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘A curse is on anyone who won’t listen to the words of this covenant.

I gave these commands to your ancestors when I pulled them out of Egypt, out of that iron furnace.’ I told them, ‘Listen to me and do everything I’m telling you. Then you’ll be my people, and I’ll be your God.
That way I can keep the oath I made to your ancestors to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, the land you have today.’” I answered, “Amen, LORD.”
The LORD told me, “Announce every word of this in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem: ‘Listen to the words of this covenant and live by them.
From the day I brought your ancestors out of Egypt to this very day, I’ve been warning you in earnest, up early and saying again and again, “Listen to me.”

But they didn’t obey or even turn an ear my way. Each one followed their own stubborn, evil heart. So I brought down on them everything this covenant said would happen. I told them what to do, and they didn’t do it.’”
The LORD said to me, “There’s a conspiracy among the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem.

They’re right back to the wrong their ancestors did when they refused to listen to me. They’ve gone off to serve other gods. The families of Israel and Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.
So the LORD says, ‘Look, I’m bringing disaster on them, and they won’t be able to get away from it. They’ll cry out to me, but I won’t listen.
Then the towns of Judah and the people of Jerusalem will run to the gods they burn incense to and cry out to them. Those gods won’t save them at all when trouble comes.
Judah, you’ve got as many gods as you’ve got towns. Jerusalem, you’ve set up as many altars to that shameful thing as you’ve got streets, altars for burning incense to Baal.’
“So don’t pray for these people. Don’t cry out or pray on their behalf. I won’t listen when they cry to me because they’re in trouble.
What’s my beloved doing in my house when she’s acted indecently with so many? The sacred meat has been taken away from you. You do wrong, and then you celebrate.”
The LORD called you “a green olive tree, beautiful and full of fine fruit.” Now with a mighty roar he’s lit it on fire, and its branches are broken.
The LORD of Armies, who planted you, has declared disaster against you. The families of Israel and Judah brought this on themselves by doing evil and making me angry with their incense to Baal.
The LORD let me in on it, so I knew. You showed me what they were doing.

But I was like a gentle lamb being led to slaughter. I had no clue they were plotting against me, saying, “Let’s wreck the tree, fruit and all. Cut him off from the land of the living so nobody remembers his name.”
LORD of Armies, you judge fairly and test the heart and mind. I’ll see you take vengeance on them, because you’re the one I’ve laid my case before.
“So here’s what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth who want you dead. They tell you, ‘If you keep prophesying in the LORD’s name, we’ll kill you.’
So the LORD of Armies says, ‘Watch, I’ll punish them. The young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die of famine.
None of them will be left. I’ll bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year I call them to account.’”
